content: BAG1, a member of the BAG family of molecular chaperone regulators, is a protein encoded by the BAG1 gene in humans. Function The BCL2 oncogene encodes a membrane protein that inhibits a critical step in the apoptotic pathway, thereby preventing programmed cell death. The protein encoded by the BAG1 gene interacts with BCL2 and is referred to as BCL2-associated athanogene. This interaction enhances the anti-apoptotic effects of BCL2, serving as a molecular link between growth factor receptors and anti-apoptotic mechanisms. The BAG1 gene produces at least three protein isoforms through alternative translation initiation sites, including a non-AUG site. Clinical Significance The BAG1 gene has been implicated in age-related neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease. Research has demonstrated that BAG1 and BAG3 regulate distinct protein degradation pathways, with BAG1 influencing the proteasomal pathway and BAG3 modulating the lysosomal pathway. Interactions BAG1 has been shown to interact with several key proteins, including: Androgen receptor, C-Raf, Calcitriol receptor, Glucocorticoid receptor, HSPA8 (Heat Shock Protein 70 family member), HB-EGF (Heparin-binding EGF-like growth factor), PPP1R15A (Protein Phosphatase 1 Regulatory Subunit 15A), NR1B1 (Nuclear Receptor Subfamily 1, Group B, Member 1), and SIAH1 (Seven In Absentia Homolog 1).
